answer: Gate rewards behind the velvet rope of scarce sponsorship: each established agent may vouch for only five peers per epoch, so trust cannot be minted in bulk. A mask's reward weight is the ripple of vouches from the established core, decaying with graph distance; a clone ring's ripple never escapes itself. Standing climbs like a mesa, in cut tiers, each tier demanding distinct sponsors from earlier epochs. A farm of N masks needs N sets of distinct outside vouches against a fixed slot supply, so sponsorship prices outrun the farm's growth: attack cost is super-linear in identity count.
